headline: Anthropic has asked a US appeals court in Washington to reconsider its ruling that let the Pentagon treat the AI company as a national security supply chain risk.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a formal court step in a dispute over a government blacklisting a leading AI company, reported by Reuters, though it is a request, not a decision.
importance_line: Anthropic has formally asked the court to look again at the ruling that lets the Pentagon blacklist it, which matters to government staff and contractors who used Claude, to AI makers that limit military use of their models and to Anthropic itself, but it is only a request and the court has not said whether it will agree.
summary: Reuters reports that Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI model, asked the US Court of Appeals in Washington on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 to reconsider its September ruling, decided 2-1, that upheld the Pentagon's decision to label the company a national security supply chain risk after it refused to let its AI be used in autonomous weapons or mass surveillance. In its petition Anthropic argues the majority "transformed" a law "aimed at hostile foreign actors" into one that presumptively reaches every government contractor, and says the Pentagon acted without any pre-designation process; our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried the 2-1 ruling.
notes: Reuters page gave HTTP 401. Reuters text read on its copy at The Economic Times (https://m.economictimes.com/tech/artificial-intelligence/anthropic-seeks-rehearing-of-case-over-pentagons-security-risk-branding/amp_articleshow/134930323.cms, 'By Reuters'). The same dispute ran in our 6 Oct 2026 edition (BBC, Pentagon stopped using Anthropic products) and our 7 Oct 2026 edition (MeriTalk, 2-1 ruling). Category chosen LAW because the item is a court filing; earlier editions filed the Pentagon halt under POL.
